ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: in the figure, the vertical axis is flagpole shadow length, with the unit being meters; the horizontal axis is Beijing time, marking about 11:30, 11:35, 11:40, 11:45, 11:50, 11:55, 12:00, and 12:05. The question stem gives the flagpole height as 5 m, so the shortest shadow length is about equal to the flagpole height. Reasoning: the shortest shadow in a day corresponds to local noon, so local noon at this place occurs at about 11:40 Beijing time, 20 minutes earlier than 12:00 Beijing time. The earlier the local time, the farther east the longitude; 20 minutes corresponds to a longitude difference of about 5°, so this place is at about 125°E. The date is around September 23, close to the autumnal equinox, when the direct solar point is on the equator; at noon, the flagpole height is 5 m and the shadow length is 5 m, tan solar altitude angle = 5/5 = 1, so the solar altitude angle is about 45°. From the noon solar altitude on the autumnal equinox, the latitude can be inferred to be about 45°N. 45°N, 125°E is located in Northeast China. Northeast China has broad plains, concentrated and contiguous cultivated land, and relatively low population density; it is an important commodity grain base and is suitable for mechanized and large-scale operation, so the level of agricultural mechanization and scale in this region is high.

Since the shortest shadow marks local noon, local noon is 20 minutes earlier than Beijing time noon, so the site is about 5° east of 120°E, near 125°E. At the equinox, with pole height 5 m and noon shadow 5 m, tan H = 1, so H ≈ 45°, giving latitude about 45°N. Locate 45°N, 125°E in Northeast China. Then apply regional agricultural knowledge: Northeast China has flat plains, large cultivated areas, relatively low population density and commodity grain production, so agriculture has high mechanization and large-scale operation.
